newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland to try to put right 1949 Swiss banks deal.
newsitem.headline: Poland to try to put right 1949 Swiss banks deal.

text.p: Poland said on Tuesday its former communist rulers had acted wrongly in using money left in Swiss banks by Poles who died in World War Two, including Jews killed in the Holocaust, and announced plans to put matters right.

Foreign Minister Dariusz Rosati spoke after the cabinet studied the results of a probe into a 1949 deal under which Switzerland used Polish funds in unclaimed Swiss bank accounts as part of a compensation deal for assets seized by the communists.

"The 1949 agreement contained many legal flaws...it was not ratified by the Polish parliament...the way in which the money was accepted was unlawful as inheritance procedures were not carried out," Rosati told a news conference.
"We cannot regard this matter as closed," he added.

Polish authorities launched the probe after Senator Alfonse D'Amato, head of the U.S. Senate Banking Committee, accused Switzerland last year of giving money to Poland from unclaimed Jewish accounts as part of an accord on compensating Swiss nationals whose assets had been seized in communist Poland.
Rosati said the inter-ministerial committee had established that under the 1949 deal, Swiss citizens were to be given 53.5 million Swiss francs ($40 million) in compensation.
Most was to come from Polish exports, largely of coal, but the rest was to be paid out of Polish citizens' Swiss accounts unclaimed for five years, he said.
He said 16,000 Swiss francs from such accounts, received in 1960, had gone to compensate Swiss claimants, while another 464,000 francs had been paid into the Polish budget in 1975.
Tuesday's cabinet meeting agreed that Poland should now launch legal inheritance procedures for the unclaimed accounts, which would involve trying to identify any surviving heirs.
"There is also a suggestion that sums for which no heirs can be found should be used to commemorate the victims of World War Two," Rosati said.
The accounts were not fully identified when Switzerland handed over the money and Rosati said Warsaw's justice minister would ask Swiss authorities for details of their owners.
It is likely that many of the unclaimed Polish accounts were opened by Jews. Most of Poland's 3.5 million Jewish community were killed by the Nazis during World War Two.

Meanwhile, the Swiss government, under pressure by Jewish groups to make restitution for alleged Swiss profiteering from the Holocaust, said on Tuesday it wanted to use dormant Swiss bank accounts to create a Holocaust memorial fund.
The Swiss Federal Council, or cabinet, said it wanted dormant bank accounts totalling around 40 million Swiss francs to be "put to a proper use".
The Swiss government insists such a fund would not be an admission that Switzerland and its secretive banks profited from the war. ($1=1.3555 Swiss Franc)
